questions.question_text: When does a useEffect cleanup function run?

choices.text: Before the effect re-runs and on unmount

questions.question_text: Why must you include every value read inside an effect in its dependency array?

choices.text: So the effect sees current values instead of a stale closure
So React can skip rendering the component
So the cleanup function never runs

questions.question_text: Calling a setState updater with the same primitive value typically:

choices.text: Bails out of re-rendering that state update

questions.question_text: Implement solve(input) where input is JSON {count: number}. Return JSON {count: count+1} as if applying a useState increment.
An effect that fetches on every keystroke has [query] as deps and no abort. Users see stale results overwrite fresh ones. What is going wrong?

reference_answer.text: In-flight requests race; a slower older request can resolve last. Abort the previous fetch or ignore stale responses (sequence id / AbortController).
rubric_points: Identifies request race or stale response
Mentions abort or ignoring outdated results
Ties the bug to the effect re-running on query change

questions.question_text: A teammate puts an object literal in a useEffect dependency array and the effect loops. What should they do instead?

reference_answer.text: Object literals get a new reference each render. Depend on primitive fields, memoize the object, or compare serialized keys.
rubric_points: Identifies new object identity each render
Explains why that stops the loop

questions.question_text: A dashboard refetches the same user profile in five child components after every navigation. Explain what is going wrong and how you would fix it.

reference_answer.text: Multiple isolated effects or prop drilling cause duplicate requests. Lift data fetching to a shared cache/provider or use a data library with request deduplication.

A teammate wants every FastAPI endpoint declared async even when it only performs blocking DB calls. Defend or push back.

reference_answer.text: Blind async on blocking work can reduce throughput; use async for truly non-blocking I/O or run blocking work in a threadpool.
rubric_points: Explains blocking work inside async endpoints
Connects recommendation to event loop behavior

questions.question_text: Fix the function so it returns the unique values preserving order.
Which index type is the default B-tree best suited for?

choices.text: Equality and range comparisons on sortable columns

questions.question_text: A report joins users to orders and unexpectedly drops users with zero orders. What join type is likely wrong, and what should you use instead?

reference_answer.text: INNER JOIN drops non-matching users. Use LEFT JOIN from users to orders (and aggregate carefully) to keep users with zero orders.
rubric_points: Identifies INNER JOIN filtering unmatched rows
Recommends LEFT/OUTER JOIN from the driving table
Mentions aggregation or COALESCE for zero counts

questions.question_text: What does READ COMMITTED prevent that READ UNCOMMITTED would allow?

choices.text: Dirty reads of uncommitted writes from other transactions

questions.question_text: EXPLAIN shows Seq Scan on a 20M-row table filtered by email = $1. What are two likely causes?

reference_answer.text: Missing index on email, or planner estimates that a sequential scan is cheaper (bad stats, low selectivity, wrong type cast preventing index use).
rubric_points: Suggests EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) or CREATE INDEX verification

questions.question_text: What is the main goal of normalizing to 3NF?

choices.text: Reduce redundant data and update anomalies via dependency clarity
Always maximize join count for performance
Store every attribute as JSON blobs
